research.official_title: AI-based solution to detect and mitigate APT malware
research.description: An investigation of whether semantic representations of system provenance events, combined with a benign-trained autoencoder, can prioritise anomalous behaviour relevant to Advanced Persistent Threats. Detection evidence is preliminary; mitigation is not yet implemented or evaluated.
research.current_activity: Consolidating the E5 provenance ablation results and preparing the E7 multiple-seed reproducibility study.
research.next_activity: E7 — repeat selected configurations with seeds 42, 123 and 456 and report mean, standard deviation and individual outcomes.
research.primary_operating_point: P99 of benign validation reconstruction error
research.implementation_note: Roadmap activity counts describe implementation progress only. No dissertation completion percentage is estimated.

leaderboard.name: Approximately matched-update unique-description training
leaderboard.research_question: Can unique-description training be matched to the original optimiser-update budget while improving anomaly prioritisation?
leaderboard.hypothesis: Approximately matching the number of optimiser updates will provide a fair comparison between frequency-preserving and unique-description training.

leaderboard.name: Unique-description training
leaderboard.research_question: Does deduplicating benign training descriptions reduce frequency dominance and improve anomaly ranking?
leaderboard.hypothesis: Training on unique descriptions will prevent the most frequent template from dominating the reconstruction objective.

leaderboard.name: Provenance ablation — full provenance
leaderboard.representation: Operations, entity attributes and explicit directed provenance relationships
leaderboard.research_question: Do explicit directed provenance relationships add detection value beyond operations and entity attributes?
leaderboard.hypothesis: Full provenance will improve observed Average Precision relative to the entity-based representation.

leaderboard.name: Original frequency-preserving autoencoder
leaderboard.research_question: Can a benign-trained autoencoder over frozen MiniLM embeddings detect anomalous provenance events?
leaderboard.hypothesis: A bottleneck autoencoder will assign higher reconstruction error to events unlike benign training activity.

leaderboard.name: Frequency-weighted training
leaderboard.research_question: Does down-weighting frequent descriptions improve the benign reconstruction objective?
leaderboard.hypothesis: Frequency weighting with 1/sqrt(frequency) will balance learning without discarding repeated benign behaviour.

leaderboard.name: Provenance ablation — operations and entities
leaderboard.representation: Operations plus process and artifact attributes, without explicit directed relationships
leaderboard.research_question: Do entity attributes resolve operation-only ambiguity without explicit directed relationships?
leaderboard.hypothesis: Adding process and artifact attributes will eliminate observed description conflicts and improve detection.

findings.title: Operation-only representations are ambiguous
findings.research_question: Can operation names alone distinguish malicious from benign provenance events?
findings.observation: All 70 original positive events share an operation-only description with 8,393 negatively labelled events. E5-A and B5 detect 0 original positives at P99.
findings.evidence: E5-A ROC-AUC 0.826367, AP 0.003219, recall 0% at P99. B5 ROC-AUC 0.826134, AP 0.003212, recall 0%. Representation conflict analysis: 1 conflicting description covering 8,463 records, including all 70 positives.
findings.interpretation: Operation names alone cannot separate events that differ only in entities or graph context. Entity and relationship information is necessary in this dataset.
findings.limitations: The conflict analysis measures exact-description collisions and does not prove that all ambiguous events are semantically indistinguishable.

findings.title: One benign description dominates training frequency
findings.research_question: Is the benign training distribution dominated by a small number of recurring descriptions?
findings.observation: A single description occurs 72,986 times, representing approximately 73.23% of the 99,665 benign training events.
findings.evidence: E2-D and E5 training logs: 72,986 / 99,665 = 73.23%. Only 13,029 unique descriptions occur in training.
findings.interpretation: Frequency-preserving training can allow one recurring benign template to dominate the reconstruction objective, motivating unique-description and frequency-weighted variants.
findings.limitations: Frequency dominance is measured on the training partition only and may reflect the collection scenario rather than general benign behaviour.

findings.title: Frequency-balanced training improves observed anomaly ranking
findings.research_question: Does approximately matched-update unique-description training improve anomaly ranking?
findings.observation: E2-D achieves ROC-AUC 0.995584 and AP 0.109080, the strongest observed ranking, compared with E2-A at 0.984482 and 0.020832.
findings.evidence: E2-D vs E2-A on the same attack-test partition with original labels. AP is approximately 5.2 times higher for E2-D.
findings.interpretation: Reducing frequency dominance while matching optimiser updates substantially improves anomaly ranking in this single-seed experiment.
findings.limitations: Only seed 42 is available. The comparison has not been repeated across seeds or independent scenarios.

findings.title: Alert prioritisation is materially better for E2-D
findings.research_question: How many original positives are recovered within small analyst alert budgets?
findings.observation: E2-D identifies 46 of 70 original positives within the top 500 alerts, compared with 0 for E2-A, 7 for E2-B and 0 for E2-C.
findings.evidence: Tie-aware alert-budget analysis: E2-D 5/100/200/500 = 5/16/29/46 true positives; E2-A and E2-C recover none until budget 1,000.
findings.interpretation: Anomaly ranking quality has a large practical effect on analyst workload, even when threshold-based precision remains low.
findings.limitations: The budgets are measured points, not interpolated estimates. Absolute precision within 500 alerts is 9.2% for E2-D.

findings.title: Full provenance improves observed Average Precision
findings.research_question: Do entity attributes and explicit provenance relationships improve detection over operations alone?
findings.observation: E5-C achieves AP 0.021743 versus 0.018724 for E5-B and 0.003219 for E5-A. The E5-C advantage over E5-B is approximately 16.1%.
findings.interpretation: Full provenance provides the best observed AP among the controlled E5 configurations, while entity attributes account for most of the improvement over operations alone.
findings.limitations: The ablation changes multiple textual properties at once; it does not isolate the causal contribution of graph relationships. E5-C is worse than E5-B on benign FPR, attack FPR, precision and F1 at P99.

findings.title: Threshold choice trades false positives against contextual recall
findings.research_question: How sensitive are operational metrics to validation-derived threshold choice?
findings.observation: For E2-D, moving from P99 to P99.95 reduces false positives from 8,628 to 2,339 while contextual recall falls from 77.33% to 49.33%; original recall remains 100%.
findings.evidence: P99 threshold 0.0002799674, precision 0.805%, benign FPR 0.754%. P99.95 threshold 0.0005867360, precision 2.906%, benign FPR 0.126%.
findings.interpretation: Higher percentiles can substantially reduce alert volume, but the trade-off is context-dependent and must be evaluated against analyst capacity and missed-context risk.
findings.limitations: P99.95 was examined retrospectively after attack-test inspection and is exploratory, not an independently validated deployment threshold.

limitations.title: Severe class imbalance
limitations.detail: The attack test contains 70 original positive events among 100,892 events (approximately 0.0694%). Precision is therefore highly sensitive to false positives.
limitations.mitigation: Report precision-recall metrics, alert budgets and false-positive counts rather than accuracy alone.

limitations.title: Only 70 original positive annotations
limitations.detail: All original-positive conclusions depend on 70 edge-derived annotations. A small number of missed or mislabelled events could materially change recall estimates.
limitations.mitigation: Treat results as preliminary and seek annotation review or additional scenarios.

limitations.title: Positives concentrated in two tactics
limitations.detail: Original positives comprise 69 credentialAccess events and 1 defenceEvasion event. Detection performance for other MITRE ATT&CK tactics is not established by original labels.
limitations.mitigation: Use contextual tactics only as derived indicators and collect broader labelled scenarios.

limitations.title: Contextual labels are derived indicators
limitations.detail: The 225 contextual positives are derived from connected provenance nodes, not independent ground-truth event annotations.
limitations.mitigation: Keep original and contextual metrics separate; never present contextual recall as confirmed attack detection.

limitations.title: Repeated exploratory evaluation of Phase 2
limitations.detail: The attack-test partition has been inspected repeatedly across variants and thresholds, creating selection and overfitting risk.
limitations.mitigation: Label retrospective analyses explicitly and require independent scenario validation.

journal.title: Provenance ablation and alert-prioritisation analysis
journal.summary: Completed the E5 representation ablation, consolidated E2 threshold and alert-budget analyses, and prepared the reproducibility study.
journal.body:
## Activities completed

- Completed the controlled E5 provenance representation ablation across operation-only (E5-A), operations plus entity attributes (E5-B) and full directed provenance (E5-C).
- Consolidated the E2-D threshold sensitivity results for validation percentiles P95 through P100.
- Consolidated the tie-aware alert-prioritisation analysis for E2-A through E2-D.
- Reviewed per-tactic recall, seen/unseen description performance and representation conflicts.
- Began the read-only research dashboard under `web/` to make the artifacts reviewable by supervisors.

## Experiments executed

- **E5-A**: operation-only autoencoder, seed 42, 100 epochs.
- **E5-B**: operations and entity attributes, seed 42, 100 epochs.
- **E5-C**: full provenance, seed 42, 100 epochs.
- **E2-T**: analytical percentile sweep over the existing E2 predictions.
- **E2-R**: analytical alert-budget simulation over the existing E2 predictions.

## Findings

- Operation-only representations are highly ambiguous: all 70 original positives share a description with 8,393 negatively labelled events.
- Adding entity attributes eliminates the observed exact-description conflicts for original positives and raises AP from 0.003219 to 0.018724.
- Full provenance reaches AP 0.021743, approximately 16.1% above the entity-based representation, but is slightly worse on benign FPR, attack FPR, precision and F1 at P99.
- E2-D remains the leading anomaly ranker (ROC-AUC 0.995584, AP 0.109080) and recovers 46 of 70 original positives within the top 500 alerts.
- The P99.95 threshold reduces E2-D false positives from 8,628 to 2,339 but reduces contextual recall from 77.33% to 49.33%.

## Problems encountered

- The ablation changes text length, ordering and formatting alongside content, so it cannot isolate the causal effect of relationships alone.
- The full-provenance test set contains 283 descriptions above the 256-token encoder limit.
- Original positives remain concentrated in two ATT&CK tactics (69 credentialAccess, 1 defenceEvasion), limiting per-tactic conclusions.

## Solutions implemented

- Interpreted E5 as an overall representation comparison rather than a pure relationship ablation.
- Kept original and contextual label metrics separate in every report.
- Labelled the P99.95 operating point as retrospective and exploratory.
- Retained P99 as the primary experimental operating point.

## Decisions made

- E2-D is the leading observed model but is not designated for deployment.
- No threshold will be selected solely from attack-test performance.
- The next experiment is E7 multiple-seed reproducibility with seeds 42, 123 and 456.
- Current findings remain preliminary until multi-seed and independent-scenario evidence is available.

## Remaining questions

- Do the E2-D improvements persist across random seeds?
- Does full provenance retain its AP advantage under a matched text-length control?
- How much of the contextual-label recall gap is caused by annotation coverage rather than model error?
- Can temporal correlation reduce the false-positive volume without sacrificing original-positive recall?

## Next steps

1. Run E7 with seeds 42, 123 and 456.
2. Report mean, standard deviation and individual outcomes for ROC-AUC, AP, precision, recall and alert-budget recovery.
3. Design an independent attack-scenario validation protocol.
4. Investigate chunk-aware embeddings for descriptions above the token limit.

## Related artifacts

- `results/ablation_comparison/ablation_comparison.csv`
- `results/ablation_comparison/alert_budget_comparison.csv`
- `results/eda/ablation/representation_statistics.csv`
- `results/eda/ablation/representation_conflicts.json`
- `results/autoencoder_comparison/threshold_comparison.csv`
- `results/autoencoder_comparison/alert_budget_comparison.csv`
- `results/e2d-unique-matched/evaluation/evaluation_summary.json`

upcoming.name: Semantic nearest-neighbour baseline
upcoming.research_question: How does a simple semantic nearest-neighbour distance compare with the autoencoder?
upcoming.hypothesis: Cosine distance to the nearest benign training embedding will provide a strong, interpretable baseline.
upcoming.training_strategy: Store benign training embeddings; no parametric training.
upcoming.interpretation: Planned comparison to test whether the autoencoder adds value beyond embedding similarity.

upcoming.name: V1 versus V2 verbalisation comparison

upcoming.training_strategy: Train matched configurations on each representation.

upcoming.name: Chunk-aware embeddings
upcoming.research_question: Can chunking long descriptions reduce information loss from the 256-token encoder limit?
upcoming.hypothesis: Chunk-aware encoding will improve detection for long provenance descriptions affected by truncation.

upcoming.name: MPNet encoder comparison

upcoming.hypothesis: MPNet may capture subtle semantic differences at higher computational cost.
upcoming.interpretation: Candidate comparison, not an implemented result.

upcoming.research_question: Can correlated event sequences improve detection beyond independent event scoring?
upcoming.hypothesis: Temporal and provenance-aware grouping will reduce isolated false positives and support incident reconstruction.
upcoming.interpretation: Planned extension from event-level to sequence-level detection.
